comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Real Estate Portfolio Composition and Concentration
comparisons.peer_summary: Commercial real estate loans decreased $7.1 billion in 2024 to $65.7 billion, with office representing the largest property type concentration at 23% and California the largest state concentration at 21%.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose that their real estate loan portfolios are predominantly secured, although JPMorgan quantifies this at 84% while Bank of America describes its portfolio generally as 'secured by non-owner-occupied real estate' without providing a specific percentage. JPMorgan explicitly highlights the credit quality of its unsecured exposure as 'largely investment-grade' to diversified REITs and REOCs, whereas Bank of America emphasizes geographic concentration, noting California as the largest state concentration (21%).

Both firms highlight the high credit quality of their CRE portfolios as a risk mitigation factor.
